advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that exercises _current_revision's real body (stub GerritClient.get_change_event) so the fail-open try/except and revision extraction are covered, not only the monkeypatched shortcut.
evidence: The fail-open branch tested (line 3052) stubs _current_revision to return None directly, never triggering the real try/except in _current_revision at app.py:249
advisory.finding: The new unit tests monkeypatch appmod._current_revision entirely, so neither the real GerritClient.get_change_event call nor the asyncio.to_thread wrapping inside _superseded_by is exercised; the actual Gerrit-integration path (id shaping, revision extraction, the try/except fail-open) has no coverage.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a worker test with an event `type=='manual-rerun'` and a mismatched current revision asserting it is reviewed, not discarded.
evidence: app.py:312 adds `if force or (isinstance(event, dict) and event.get("type") == "manual-rerun")` — a two-armed carve-out
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:3061 `test_worker_does_not_discard_a_forced_rerun` sets `ev["_rebar_force"] = True`, exercising only the `force` arm
ABSENCE: no test drives an event with `type == "manual-rerun"` and a stale revision, so a regression that dropped the `manual-rerun` disjunct would discard deliberately-requested reruns undetected
advisory.finding: The `manual-rerun` type bypass branch of the staleness carve-out is untested; only the `force`/`_rebar_force` path is covered.
scenarios: A refactor or typo removes the `manual-rerun` OR-arm; manual reruns of a change whose current revision differs from the queued one get silently discarded
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring `test_worker_does_not_discard_a_forced_rerun` but setting `ev["type"] = "manual-rerun"` (no `_rebar_force`) and `_current_revision` returning a different sha, asserting `reviewed` is non-empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the queued event has no `patchSet.revision`, asserting the worker reviews it (does not discard).
evidence: app.py:260-262 adds `queued = _event_revision(event)` then `if queued is None: return None`
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:46 `_event` always sets `patchSet.revision`, so every test supplies a queued revision
ABSENCE: no test constructs an event missing `patchSet.revision`; a regression that reversed this short-circuit (e.g. treating a revisionless event as superseded) would go uncaught
advisory.finding: `_superseded_by`'s no-queued-revision branch (`if queued is None: return None`) is untested — no test drives an event whose payload lacks `patchSet.revision`.
scenarios: An event payload arrives with no `patchSet.revision`; the guard must review-it (return None) rather than discard
advisory.suggested_fix: Drive `_worker` with an event whose `patchSet` omits `revision` and assert `reviewed` is non-empty and no discard marker is emitted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that makes the real `_current_revision` catch a boundary exception (monkeypatch `GerritClient`/`get_change_event` to raise) and asserts the worker reviews the event.
evidence: test at tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:3052 does `monkeypatch.setattr(appmod, "_current_revision", lambda event, cfg: None, raising=False)` — replacing the whole helper
app.py:238-251 the real fail-open lives in `_current_revision`'s `try/except Exception` around `GerritClient(cfg).get_change_event(...)`, which the test bypasses entirely

ABSENCE: no test makes the real `_current_revision` catch a raised exception from the Gerrit boundary and return None; the code that implements the deliberate 'NEVER RAISES / fail open' contract is untested
advisory.finding: The fail-open test stubs the internal `_current_revision` to return None rather than exercising its real try/except boundary, so the actual exception-swallowing fail-open code (and the GerritClient external boundary) is never run.
scenarios: GerritClient.get_change_event raises (auth error, blip); the contract says review anyway — but the try/except that enforces this is never executed by any test
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch the external seam — `GerritClient.get_change_event` (or the lazily-imported client) — to raise, and drive the real `_current_revision`/`_superseded_by`, asserting the event is reviewed and no discard marker fires.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the current-revision staleness lookup with a timeout so a hung Gerrit read cannot stall the serial worker (the review_timeout guard does not cover _superseded_by).
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:318: `await asyncio.wait_for(_voter.review_and_vote(...), timeout=review_timeout)` — only review_and_vote is under the timeout, not the preceding _superseded_by call
_current_revision makes a blocking REST call (GerritClient(cfg).get_change_event) with no timeout parameter shown; a hung Gerrit connection blocks the thread and the worker never advances
dropped.finding: The staleness-guard current-revision lookup runs OUTSIDE the review_timeout guard, so a slow/hung Gerrit REST call (get_change_event) can stall the single serial worker indefinitely — the very head-of-line-blocking failure mode the timeout guard (bug 9d7c) was added to prevent. asyncio.to_thread moves it off the event loop but does not bound it.
dropped.suggested_fix: Wrap the _superseded_by call in its own asyncio.wait_for (or ensure GerritClient uses a request timeout), so a slow current-revision lookup fails open rather than blocking the worker.
